data.long_meaning: In Sanskrit, Ambar means 'Sky' or 'Heaven'. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ambar usually hope their child will grow to embody sky, heaven and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Ambarisha, a king mentioned in the Mahabharata, was a great devotee of Lord Vishnu. He performed a yajna (sacrifice) to please the deity, and was blessed with a divine chariot named 'Eka Ratha'. The name 'Ambar' may be derived from this reference, as it means 'sky' or 'heavenly' in Sanskrit.

Another reference to the name 'Ambar' comes from the Puranas, specifically the Skanda Purana. In this text, Ambar is mentioned as the name of a king who ruled over the Haihayas, a prominent clan in ancient India. He is described as a just and virtuous ruler who ruled during the Treta Yuga (second of the four stages of Hindu cosmology).
